title: Horizontal support/resistance zone detection + false-breakout signal
description: Currently zero support/resistance logic anywhere in this app -- Screen 3/Trigger only ever compares against yesterday's single high/low, never a zone built from repeated touches. Concrete, well-specified rules from docs/ideas.md (Elder ch. 18): a zone is a horizontal congestion area (the edges of where price repeatedly stalled, not the extreme wick), strength scored by length (2wk=minor/2mo=intermediate/2yr=major), height as % of price (~1%/~3%/>=7%), and volume traded within the zone; zones flip roles once broken (old resistance becomes new support); a false breakout (price closes beyond the zone, then closes back inside it) is a specific, high-value reversal signal with an explicit stop-placement rule (near the false breakout's own extreme). This task covers detection + strength scoring + false-breakout flagging + API exposure. Using this to tighten the existing stop-loss formula near a known zone (also logged in docs/ideas.md) is a separate, later task -- note it as a natural follow-up but don't implement it here.

checklist.step: Implement congestion-zone detection over the daily series (decide and record the exact algorithm -- e.g. clustering of touches within a tolerance band -- since the book describes the concept precisely but not a mechanical detection algorithm).
Implement the three-factor strength score (length/height/volume) per the book's thresholds.
Implement zone role-flipping (a broken zone keeps existing, inverted role) rather than discarding zones after a breakout.
Implement false-breakout detection with the explicit stop-placement reference point (the failed move's own extreme).
Tests covering: a clean multi-touch zone, a zone that flips role after breaking, and a false breakout that reverses vs. a true breakout that doesn't.
Expose zones + false-breakout flags on GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis; regenerate openapi.json/frontend types; document in docs/Analyse.md.

decisions.decision: Zone-detection algorithm (app.signals.support_resistance.detect_support_resistance_zones): (1) find swing points via a 5-bar fractal window (today plus 2 bars each side -- a bar is a swing high if its `high` equals the max of that window, a swing low if its `low` equals the min); (2) cluster each side's swing points using their own CLOSE price (not the high/low wick), via sequential 1-D clustering -- sort by price, merge a point into the running cluster if within 1% of the cluster's current mean price, else start a new cluster; (3) a cluster becomes a candidate zone only with >=2 touches spanning >=14 calendar days (below either floor, it's dropped entirely, not reported as a weak zone).
decisions.rationale: The book (Elder ch. 18, per docs/ideas.md) describes the concept precisely -- 'a horizontal congestion area... the edges of where price repeatedly stalled, not the extreme wick' -- but gives no mechanical algorithm, which this task's own checklist explicitly flags as a judgment call to make and record. Clustering on CLOSE rather than the swing bar's own high/low directly implements 'not the extreme wick' from the task's own description -- the zone's edges are where price actually settled repeatedly, not the single furthest tick. A 5-bar fractal is a simple, standard swing-point definition that doesn't require building (or depending on) the separate, not-yet-implemented backend-swing-point-detector task -- this task's depends_on is deliberately empty, so introducing a hard dependency on that unbuilt module was rejected in favor of a small self-contained fractal check. 1% cluster tolerance and the 2-touch/14-day floors are this app's own thresholds (the book gives no clustering-tolerance number at all); 14 days matches the book's own 'length: 2 weeks = minor' floor directly, so below it a cluster isn't even the weakest recognized zone. Rejected alternatives: (a) clustering on the swing bar's raw high/low instead of its close -- rejected as directly contradicting this task's own 'not the extreme wick' framing; (b) a k-means/density-based clustering algorithm instead of simple sequential merge-by-tolerance -- rejected as unnecessary complexity for a 1-D clustering problem with no natural cluster count to fit, and sequential merge is trivially auditable/hand-verifiable, which the reference-value testing bar (add-indicator skill) favors; (c) depending on backend-swing-point-detector's eventual output -- rejected since that task doesn't exist yet and this task's depends_on is empty by design.

decisions.decision: Strength scoring: length_category boundaries use the book's own three values directly (minor <60 days, intermediate 60-729 days, major >=730 days). height_category boundaries are the MIDPOINTS between the book's three anchor values (~1%/~3%/>=7%), i.e. minor <2%, intermediate 2-4.99%, major >=5% -- chosen so each anchor value itself still classifies the way the book intends (1% -> minor, 3% -> intermediate, 7% -> major). height_pct is computed against the ticker's CURRENT (latest) close, the same reference for every zone on a given call -- not each zone's own (potentially long-past) touch-era price. dollar_volume uses Elder's own explicit formula (days-in-zone x average daily volume x average price, over the zone's own touch span, 'days-in-zone' read as trading days actually present in that span) but is exposed RAW, not classified into minor/intermediate/major and not folded into strength_score numerically. strength_score (0-100) is the average of the length and height category scores only (minor=33.3, intermediate=66.7, major=100, averaged).
decisions.rationale: Length has three literal book values to use as boundaries directly -- no ambiguity there. Height only has three ANCHOR points, not stated boundaries -- the book's language is '~1% = minor, ~3% = intermediate, >=7% = major', which are points on a continuum, not a partition; using the midpoints between consecutive anchors is the natural, symmetric way to turn three anchors into three category boundaries without arbitrarily favoring one side. 'Height as % of current price' is the task's own literal wording (not '% of the zone's own historical price'), so the current-close reference was chosen over an alternative (each zone's own midpoint or touch-era price) that would make the same physical zone's classification depend on when it happened to form rather than what it means for the stock today -- current-price reference also makes every zone on a single API response directly comparable to each other. dollar_volume has an explicit, unambiguous FORMULA from the book but the book gives no absolute dollar-value thresholds anywhere to classify a computed number into minor/intermediate/major (unlike length/height, which do have anchor values) -- inventing thresholds with no textual basis would be a much weaker judgment call than the length/height ones, which at least start from the book's own numbers, so it's exposed as a raw, informational field instead (documented explicitly in the field description so a client knows why). Rejected alternatives: (a) classifying dollar_volume by comparing it to the ticker's own trailing average dollar volume (a relative rather than absolute threshold) -- considered, but rejected as introducing yet another invented parameter (what trailing window? what ratio counts as 'high'?) for a field the book never asks to be categorized at all, only computed; (b) folding a volume factor into strength_score via such a relative comparison -- rejected for the same reason, and because it would make strength_score depend on an extra invented parameter beyond the two (length/height) the book's own anchor values actually support.

decisions.decision: Role-flipping and false-breakout scanning: after a zone forms, scan daily closes strictly after its last touch date. A close beyond the zone ('breached') opens a 10-trading-day confirmation window: if price closes back inside [lower, upper] within that window, it's recorded as a false breakout (FalseBreakout.extreme_price = the failed move's own highest high / lowest low) and the zone's role is UNCHANGED, with scanning continuing past the reentry bar (so a zone can accumulate several false-breakout episodes over time -- only the most recent is retained). If no reentry occurs within the window, the break is confirmed: `broken=True`, `break_date` set, and role flips (resistance<->support) -- scanning then STOPS, so this implementation tracks at most one confirmed role flip per zone (a zone that's already flipped isn't scanned further for a second flip). A confirmed break and an earlier, separate false-breakout episode can coexist on the same zone (the false_breakout field is not cleared when a later true break occurs).
decisions.rationale: The book gives the CONCEPT (false breakout = closes beyond then closes back inside; true breakout flips the zone's role) but no numeric confirmation window -- 10 trading days is this app's own choice, picked as a short-but-not-trivial window (two calendar weeks) that gives a breakout a real chance to prove itself false without letting an old, stale zone be 'broken' by a much later, unrelated price move that happens to close beyond its old bounds. Stopping at the first confirmed flip (rather than tracking a chain of repeated flips) keeps the implementation's behavior fully covered by this task's own checklist test requirement ('a zone that flips role after breaking') without open-ended scope creep into full zone-lifecycle re-evaluation after a flip, which is a natural, separable follow-up (see the API-exposure/protective_stop follow-up decision below for the same reasoning applied at the feature level) -- not something the book's own description requires this task to solve. Allowing false_breakout and broken=True to coexist (rather than clearing false_breakout once a later real break occurs) was chosen because they describe two genuinely different, independently-true historical facts about the zone (an earlier failed attempt, and a later successful one) -- clearing the field would silently discard real information a client might want (e.g. 'this zone survived one attack before finally breaking'). Rejected alternatives: (a) using volume to help distinguish true vs. false breakouts (the book does mention heavy volume confirms true breakouts, light volume marks false ones) -- rejected for this task's algorithm since the book's own PRICE-ACTION definition (closes beyond, then closes back inside) is already a complete, checkable rule on its own per this task's description ('a false breakout = price closes beyond support/resistance, then closes back inside the zone'), and folding in a volume heuristic would add another invented threshold without the book giving one specifically for this confirmation; (b) continuing to scan for further flips after the first one -- rejected as unnecessary for satisfying this task's own checklist/test requirements and better left as a deliberate follow-up if ever needed.

decisions.decision: Cap detect_support_resistance_zones() at the 15 strongest zones (by strength_score, then touch_count, then most-recent last_touch_date, all descending) rather than returning every detected cluster.
decisions.rationale: A multi-year daily history can produce dozens of small, low-significance swing-point clusters (especially with the 1% clustering tolerance and 2-touch/14-day floors chosen above) -- returning all of them would bloat the API payload and give a consuming client (a future chart overlay, per the frontend-support-resistance-overlay follow-up task already on the board) no natural way to know which ones actually matter. Capping by strength_score (this task's own composite of the book's length/height factors) surfaces the zones Elder's own methodology considers most significant first, matching how a technical trader would actually prioritize S/R levels on a chart (a handful of major/intermediate zones, not every minor blip). Rejected alternatives: (a) no cap at all -- rejected as an unbounded response size for a long-history ticker with no benefit, since a client showing more than ~15 zones on one chart would be unreadable anyway; (b) a much smaller cap (e.g. 5) -- rejected as potentially hiding a real major zone that happens to rank 6th-15th by this task's own scoring, given the deliberately conservative (book-anchor-derived) category boundaries above.

decisions.decision: Compute support_resistance_zones directly in app.api.routers.stocks.get_analysis (calling app.signals.support_resistance.detect_support_resistance_zones(daily_ohlcv) once), rather than inside app.signals.engine.analyse()/analyse_history() alongside the other indicators dict entries.
decisions.rationale: This task's own checklist scopes exposure to GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis only ('Expose zones + false-breakout flags on GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis'), not GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators -- unlike channel_upper/channel_lower (backend-channel-envelope-exposure), which are per-bar scalar values both endpoints need and which analyse_history()'s existing precompute-and-slice pattern was built specifically to share across up to thousands of per-bar analyse() calls. Zone detection is a whole-history swing/cluster/breakout pass, not a per-bar scalar -- folding it into analyse() would pay that whole-history cost on every single one of analyse_history()'s per-bar calls (each call would redundantly re-run the entire detection pipeline over its own growing prefix) for a consumer (GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators) that this task never asked to expose zones to at all. Computing it once, directly in get_analysis, avoids that entirely and keeps the change additive and narrowly scoped, matching this task's explicit 'detection + strength scoring + false-breakout flagging + API exposure ONLY' framing. Rejected alternative: add it to analyse()'s indicators/screens dicts (mirroring the channel_upper/channel_lower precedent exactly) -- rejected specifically because that precedent's own rationale (shared per-bar cost across two endpoints) doesn't apply here; doing so anyway would silently make GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's response shape change too (an unrequested, out-of-scope API surface expansion) or require extra plumbing to suppress it there, neither of which this task's checklist calls for.

decisions.decision: Zones are exposed as pure informational context on AnalysisResponse.support_resistance_zones only -- NOT wired into Screen 1/2/3, the Impulse gate, confidence scoring, or app.portfolio.risk.protective_stop's stop-loss formula. No separate follow-up task filed for the protective_stop tightening idea (docs/ideas.md's own 'ties directly into existing app logic... tighten docs/Analyse.md §7's stop-loss calculation when price nears a known S/R zone' note).
decisions.rationale: This task's own description is explicit that using zones to tighten protective_stop is a separate, later task, out of scope here ('This task covers detection + strength scoring + false-breakout flagging + API exposure... Using this to tighten the existing stop-loss formula near a known zone... is a separate, later task -- note it as a natural follow-up but don't implement it here'), and offers a choice between filing a tracked follow-up task or simply noting it in a decisions entry -- this entry is that note. A dedicated follow-up task wasn't filed because the idea is already durably tracked on the board twice over: docs/ideas.md's own 'Missing entirely: horizontal support/resistance' entry already describes the protective_stop tie-in explicitly, and this task's own `references`/description will remain visible to next-task/a future session even once this task moves to docs/tasks/done/. Filing a redundant `<id>-followups` task (the pattern this repo otherwise uses for PR-review findings) was judged unnecessary scope-tracking overhead for an idea that's already this well-documented in two other durable places, unlike a PR-review finding which would otherwise vanish once the PR merges.

comments.summary: Efficiency: detect_support_resistance_zones runs the full O(n) break/false-breakout scan and dollar_volume window computation for every candidate cluster before sorting by strength_score and truncating to max_zones (15), even though the sort key only depends on the cheap length/height categories -- a ~20yr history produces ~104 candidates while only 15 survive, so most of that scan work is thrown away on every call for a long-history ticker. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-support-resistance-followups.

docs/architecture/Backend.md's module-layout tree wasn't updated to list the new app/signals/support_resistance.py module, unlike prior tasks (autoenvelope.py, _validation.py) that updated this same list when adding a new module. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-support-resistance-followups.

_cluster_touches's sequential merge-by-running-mean can chain: each new point is compared against the cluster's current (shifting) mean, not its original anchor, so an unbroken sequence of touches each within 1% of the running mean can end up spanning noticeably more than 1% end-to-end. Not a bug (upper/lower are still the cluster's real extremes) but this known limitation isn't acknowledged in the task's decisions entry. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-support-resistance-followups.

review.notes: Full review. Tests: backend pytest --cov=app -- 598 passed, app/signals/support_resistance.py 100% line+branch, overall 99.88% (gate 90%), no regression. Frontend vitest run --coverage -- 349 passed, overall ~99.7% (gate 90%). Static analysis: backend ruff + mypy clean; frontend eslint + tsc clean. Re-ran python scripts/export_openapi.py and yarn generate:api-types against the checked-out branch -- both byte-for-byte identical to the committed backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts, genuinely regenerated not hand-edited. Elder-methodology scrutiny: false-breakout detection checks close only (breach and reentry), never high/low -- confirmed it requires a close beyond the zone AND a later close back inside, not a wick. Role-flip only fires on a confirmed break (no reentry within the 10-day window); a false breakout leaves role unchanged, verified against both unit and integration tests exercising both paths on the same fixture. Length thresholds (14/60/730 days) match the book's 2wk/2mo/2yr anchors directly (unambiguous). Height thresholds (2%/5% boundaries around 1%/3%/7% anchors) are a reasonable midpoint interpretation of the book's anchor-only guidance, and boundary tests confirm each anchor classifies as the book intends. No look-ahead bias: the module is called once per /analysis request over the full available history to produce a current-moment snapshot, not a per-bar walk-forward loop (it's explicitly not wired into analyse()/analyse_history()), so the fractal window's symmetric lookback/lookforward is the standard, correct swing-point definition here, not a leak of future data into a historical per-date determination. The zone-detection algorithm (5-bar fractal + close-price clustering at 1% tolerance + 2-touch/14-day floor) is a reasonable, well-justified interpretation of 'congestion area... not the extreme wick', backed by six decisions entries each with rejected alternatives, meeting CLAUDE.md's decision-memory bar. Router-placement (computing zones directly in get_analysis rather than inside analyse()/analyse_history()) is reasonable and consistent with how this codebase already distinguishes 'shared per-bar scalar, worth precomputing' (channel_upper/channel_lower) from 'whole-history, single-consumer computation' (this one, no second consumer exists). Checklist<->decisions cross-check: the one 'decide X' checklist item (the detection algorithm) has a corresponding decisions entry; every other judgment call implicit in the checklist is also backed by its own entry -- no gap. docs/Analyse.md and docs/architecture/API.md both updated with real content. No UI surface: this PR only adds a backend module + schema/route field + regenerated frontend types + an MSW mock fixture no component currently reads -- browser walkthrough and e2e-test explicitly skipped, no UI to exercise. Ran code-review (medium) against the diff: one real non-blocking efficiency finding (see comments), no correctness bugs. Three non-blocking findings recorded above and tracked on docs/tasks/backend-support-resistance-followups.json per the autonomous-pipeline rule.
